page: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the EPDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 154 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities for standard workloads. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the server in the middle 50% tier. Large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations also perform at average levels, alongside single-threaded gzip compression and PassMark database operations. However, the server exhibits weaker performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core suites, bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET operations. Cryptographic performance is particularly limited, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 10%, and LLM inference tasks also registering in the poor performance tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4pds_v5 offers a dense memory profile on an ARM architecture, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance vector or matrix extensions. Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and local storage, this server is suitable for relational databases, caching layers, and memory-optimized general-purpose applications that benefit from dedicated physical cores and local disk caching without requiring heavy cryptographic or mathematical computation.
